question: Should memory-core introduce default-on per-user memory isolation now, and what identity, config, legacy-memory, and fallback behavior should be the supported security contract?
rationale: The PR defines a new privacy boundary and default config behavior for existing memory search/get installs; automation can identify defects but cannot choose the permanent product and upgrade policy.

options.title: Fix and keep default-on isolation
options.body: Require absent-config identity isolation, implement or remove every accepted option, document upgrade behavior, and require redacted builtin plus QMD two-user proof before merge.

options.title: Make isolation explicit opt-in first
options.body: Reduce upgrade risk by defaulting existing installs to shared memory until a separate maintainer-approved migration and proof plan is ready.

options.title: Defer to the canonical tracker
options.body: Pause this branch and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/63550 as the design owner until the memory privacy contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Fix and keep default-on isolation
recommendation.body: Require absent-config identity isolation, implement or remove every accepted option, document upgrade behavior, and require redacted builtin plus QMD two-user proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory search and host SDK history plus current related memory cleanup make this the strongest available routing candidate.
